items.text: CNBC (8 hours ago) confirmed: Brent crude, the global oil price benchmark, is down almost 19% for the month of May. items.bold: TRUMP'S FOUR MOU CONDITIONS (CNBC confirmed): Nuclear never + Hormuz without tolls + remove mines + US destroys enriched uranium under rubble.
items.text: CNBC (8 hours ago) confirmed Trump's four conditions for MOU sign-off: (1) Tehran must agree it will never have a nuclear weapon. (2) Must immediately open Hormuz to unrestricted traffic in both directions without tolls. (3) Must agree to remove any remaining mines in the strait. (4) Must agree to allow the US to unearth and destroy its enriched uranium buried under rubble from US and Israeli attacks. Condition 4 is the most significant new detail: "unearth and destroy enriched uranium buried under rubble" acknowledges that US/Israeli strikes have already buried Iranian uranium stockpiles. This is a logistics-and-verification demand, not just a political demand — it requires physical access to Iran's territory. Condition 2 directly contradicts the Iran state TV claim (Iran+Oman manage Hormuz) — Rubio criteria "without tolls" is now formally Trump's signed condition. Iran officials: will only discuss nuclear-related clauses once Phase 1 MOU is cemented. The sequencing gap: Iran wants Phase 1 first, then nuclear. Trump wants nuclear conditions in the MOU itself.

items.bold: UBS: "Little evidence of any short-term improvement in vessel traffic." Crude loadings "extremely low." Hormuz effectively still closed.
items.text: CNBC (17 hours ago) confirmed: despite renewed prospects for peace, strikes continued Thursday with Iranian forces firing ballistic missiles at Kuwait and sending attack drones toward the Strait. Noting the attacks, UBS said there is still "little evidence" of any short-term improvement in vessel traffic or energy flows through the region. In a note, UBS analysts led by Henri Patricot (executive director, equity research, oil and gas) said crude loadings inside the Gulf remain "extremely low." The MOU is unsigned. The PGSA coordination requirement is still operational. IRGC fired warning shots at four vessels Thursday (passing "without prior coordination"). The oil price fall (-19% May) is driven entirely by deal EXPECTATION, not by any actual improvement in Hormuz traffic. This is the critical market-reality gap: Brent $92 as if the deal is done. Vessel traffic: extremely low as if the war continues. When the deal is actually signed and Hormuz begins de-mining: there will be limited additional Brent downside (already largely priced) but massive operational upside for India.

items.bold: US GAS PRICES: fell 14 cents in one day — biggest drop since November 2008 Great Recession. National average ~$4.42/gallon.
items.text: CNN (1 day ago) confirmed: the drop in US gas prices reflects the recent plunge in oil and gasoline futures in recent days as traders bet on a US-Iran deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz. The national average has declined by almost 14 cents since hitting near four-year highs of $4.56 a gallon just last week. That exceeds any decline during the pandemic in 2020 and marks the biggest one-day drop on AAA data since November 22, 2008, amid the Great Recession. This is politically critical for Trump: his approval ratings were declining on gas prices. The 14-cent single-day fall is his biggest gas price political win since the war began. Trump's political incentive to sign the MOU is now maximum — but his four conditions remain hard. The market has done his political work; he still needs Iran to meet the nuclear terms.

items.bold: IRAN: will only discuss nuclear clauses ONCE Phase 1 MOU cemented. BESSENT: declined to confirm deal details. Sequencing gap persists.
items.text: CNN (1 day ago) and CNBC confirmed the sequencing deadlock: Iranian officials warned they will only discuss nuclear-related clauses once negotiators cement the first phase of the tentative deal. Bessent declined to confirm details of the tentative agreement reached between the administration and Iran, which could extend the ceasefire and set the Strait of Hormuz on a path toward reopening. The sequencing gap: Iran: sign Phase 1 MOU (Hormuz + ceasefire) first, then discuss nuclear. Trump: nuclear conditions must be in the MOU itself before he signs. Both positions are publicly stated and directly contradictory. The resolution: likely a diplomatic bridge — nuclear "principles" in the MOU (Iran never have weapon), nuclear "specifics" (dismantlement, uranium destruction) in Phase 2. Condition 4 (US unearths and destroys buried uranium) could be a Phase 2 verification mechanism, not a Phase 1 precondition. This is the deal that both sides can sign.

military.t: TRUMP's FOUR MOU CONDITIONS (CNBC Confirmed): Nuclear Never + Hormuz Without Tolls + Remove Mines + US Destroys Buried Uranium.
military.d: CNBC (8 hours ago) confirmed Trump's four conditions for MOU sign-off: (1) Tehran must agree it will never have a nuclear weapon. (2) Must immediately open Hormuz to unrestricted traffic without tolls. (3) Must agree to remove any remaining mines. (4) Must agree to allow the US to unearth and destroy its enriched uranium buried under rubble from US and Israeli attacks. Condition 4 is the most analytically significant: US/Israeli strikes have already physically buried Iranian uranium stockpiles. Trump is demanding physical access to Iran's territory to verify and destroy the buried material. This is unprecedented — a post-war verification demand built into the ceasefire MOU conditions. Iran's sequencing response: we will discuss nuclear clauses AFTER Phase 1 MOU is signed. The bridge: put nuclear "principles" in MOU Phase 1 (Iran never have weapon, mines removed, Hormuz without tolls), put uranium verification in Phase 2 (60-day talks). This is the deal both sides can live with.

military.t: UBS: "Little Evidence" of Vessel Traffic Improvement. Crude Loadings "Extremely Low." Deal Priced, Not Done.

Crude loadings inside the Gulf remain "extremely low." This creates the most important market-reality gap of the 91-day war: Brent $92.56 = deal expectation almost fully priced. Actual vessel traffic = still at near-wartime-low levels. Implication: when the MOU is actually signed and de-mining begins (2-6 weeks), there will be limited additional Brent downside (already priced to $82-85 range). The real India benefit: operational — LPG carriers, fertiliser vessels, crude tankers resuming unrestricted Hormuz transit. That operational reality is what India needs, not just the Brent price signal.

military.t: US Gas Prices: -14 Cents One Day — Biggest Drop Since Great Recession (November 2008). National Average ~$4.42.
military.d: CNN (1 day ago) confirmed: the national average US gas price has declined by almost 14 cents since hitting near four-year highs of $4.56 a gallon just last week. That exceeds any decline during the pandemic in 2020 and marks the biggest one-day drop on AAA data since November 22, 2008, amid the Great Recession. This is Trump's biggest domestic political win of the war. Gas prices were the primary driver of his declining approval ratings (CNBC All-America Economic Survey confirmed lowest of two terms). The 14-cent single-day fall reverses weeks of political damage. Trump's political incentive to complete the MOU is now maximum — he needs the deal to claim the gas price relief. But his four conditions (especially uranium destruction) must be met before he signs. The political clock: Trump benefits from gas prices falling on deal expectation even before the MOU is signed. But if the deal collapses: gas rebounds, and his political gains evaporate.

assessment.body:
Friday 9:15 AM IST. Day 91. The last day of the worst and most extraordinary energy month India has faced since 2022.

THE BRENT PICTURE
$92.56 Friday morning — down 19% in May.
Worst monthly Brent loss since the Covid-19 pandemic.
Off 20% from 2026 peaks.
For India: Brent $92.56 vs April 30 $126 peak = $33.44/barrel fall.
Annual import bill saving: Rs 2.3 lakh crore.
The fastest monthly Brent decline since the pandemic is India's biggest energy cost relief of the war.

THE MOU STATUS
Negotiators agreed 60-day MOU. Trump has four conditions. Has not signed.
FOUR CONDITIONS:
→ Iran never have nuclear weapon
→ Hormuz immediately open, unrestricted, without tolls
→ Remove remaining mines
→ Allow US to unearth and destroy enriched uranium under rubble
Iran sequencing: nuclear only after Phase 1 MOU cemented.
The gap: Trump wants nuclear conditions in the MOU; Iran wants nuclear in Phase 2.

THE MARKET-REALITY GAP
UBS: "little evidence of short-term improvement in vessel traffic."
Crude loadings: "extremely low."
Brent $92 = deal expectation fully priced.
Actual Hormuz traffic = still at wartime lows.
When the MOU is signed: limited additional Brent downside (already priced), massive operational India benefit.

THE US GAS POLITICS
Gas prices: -14 cents in one day.
Biggest single-day drop since the Great Recession (November 2008).
Trump's biggest domestic political win of the war.
But: four conditions must be met. Iran's sequencing must be bridged.
Trump benefits from deal expectation even before signing.

INDIA's MAY 2026 — A SUMMARY
Month began: Brent $126, rupee 95.71+, Sensex crashed -2,769 pts in two days.
Month ends: Brent $92.56, Nifty above 24,000 (first since war began), deal imminent.
Net May: Rs 2.3 lakh crore annual import bill relief secured.
Petrol hiked twice (to Rs 103.54 + second hike). OMC near-breakeven on petrol at $92.
MOU unsigned but priced. The month that started as India's worst is ending as India's most hopeful.

VERDICT: Day 91 closes May 2026 — the most extraordinary month in India's energy history. Brent fell 19% in one month. The MOU exists at negotiator level. Trump's four conditions are the last obstacle. Iran's sequencing demand is the last gap. And UBS has correctly identified the market-reality gap: the deal is priced into Brent, but the ships have not moved. India goes into June with the war still on, the Hormuz still closed, and the most advanced deal framework of the 91-day conflict one Trump signature away from changing everything.

featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
